newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds skid lower, nervous about data.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds skid lower, nervous about data.

text.p: Anxious about upcoming economic data, U.S. mortgage-backed securities skidded into negative territory on a quiet Thursday session, traders said.

"It seems like the market is cleaning shop ahead of tomorrow's (economic) numbers," a Midwest trader said, referring to the heavily watched producer prices and retail sales data set for release Friday.

The market is obviously nervous about retail sales and the Producer Price Index (PPI), said a Dallas-based trader, "but I believe the real nervousness in the market is about the Consumer Price Index (CPI)."
"Most people pretty much agree that (inflation) will occur in the CPI before the PPI," she said.

Economists surveyed by Reuters last Friday projected producer prices up 0.3 percent overall in September and up 0.2 percent excluding food and energy. Retail sales for the month were forecast to have risen 0.2 percent overall and 0.3 percent excluding automobiles.
But in real terms, pass-throughs were still within their trading range, the Dallas trader said. "We traded to the top. Now, we will probably trade to the bottom."
By late Thursday, pass-throughs ranged from 2/32 to 12/32 lower.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 10/32 at 99-02/32, yielding 109 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 14/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were off 9/32 at 99-even, and FHLMCs were down 11/32 at 99-04/32.
